title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure rather than a model error. Synthetic video was used to place the faces of real, identifiable people onto pornographic footage they never appeared in, and the result was published as though it depicted them. The people affected are Dutch celebrities, presenters, athletes, officials, mayors and members of the royal family, and the reporting describes them considering or filing complaints rather than consenting to any of it.

The failure sits at the distribution layer, not in any single generation step. The material appeared on an online platform drawing roughly 13 million monthly visitors, and nothing in the reporting describes a consent check at upload or at publication, or a takedown route that removed the videos. Catching this would have required verifying that the people depicted had agreed to appear, or an authority able to force removal quickly. A parliamentary motion sought exactly that, to designate a body empowered to take deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline, which indicates no such mechanism was operating. Members of parliament were also reported to have heard nothing for months after the initial outcry.

What is not established is who produced the videos of these particular people, whether the platform knew their contents were fabricated, and whether any prosecution will follow. Complaints filed or under consideration are not findings, and the one sentence reported in the summary concerns a different case.

summary:
Multiple Dutch celebrities are considering legal action after their faces were digitally placed onto pornographic videos without consent. These manipulated deepfake videos appear on an online platform that receives approximately 13 million monthly visitors. The platform reportedly contains numerous fake pornographic videos featuring Dutch artists, television presenters, Olympic athletes, government officials, mayors, and members of the royal family. Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos disgusting and encouraged victims to file complaints.

Deepfake pornography falls under revenge porn laws and is therefore illegal in the Netherlands. According to legal experts, victims have several options including filing police reports, requesting the website be shut down, starting a class action lawsuit, or contacting hosting companies. Previously, television presenter Welmoed Sijtsma became a victim of such videos and created a documentary about her experience. A 39-year-old man from Amersfoort received a conditional sentence of 180 hours for creating fake pornographic content of Sijtsma. Lawyers warn that without government intervention, the number of fake pornographic videos featuring celebrities will continue to increase.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
